title: Polish 7/7: Criterion benchmarks, C comparison harness, multithread-scaling capstone
description:
### Summary
Criterion benchmark suite for the Rust crate, a matching C timing harness (so Rust-vs-C numbers are honest, same workloads), and the capstone: thread-scaling throughput on one shared `Ephemeris` — the demo that the stateless design earned its keep vs. C's copy-per-isolate. Results written to docs/benchmarks.md and a Performance section appended to README.md.

### Files
- `Cargo.toml` — `[dev-dependencies] criterion = "0.5"`; `[[bench]] name = "ephemeris", harness = false`
- `benches/ephemeris.rs` (new)
- `tools/bench_c.c` (new) + a target in `tools/Makefile`
- `docs/benchmarks.md` (new); `README.md` — append Performance section

### Implementation steps
1. **benches/ephemeris.rs**, four groups (each benching one call per iteration, black_box on inputs/outputs):
   - `calc_moshier`: calc(SPEED) for all 10 bodies Sun..Pluto at J2000, Moshier config — reports per-full-chart time
   - `calc_swiss`: same with Swisseph source + `ephe_path` = "ephe" (skip group gracefully with a stderr note if files absent)
   - `houses_placidus`: houses_ex2, Placidus, Zurich coords, one epoch
   - `eclipse_search`: sol_eclipse_when_glob forward from J2000, Moshier
   Also two micro groups for the known hot kernels: `nutation_iau2000b` (nutation::calc at one epoch) and `moshier_moon` (moshier moon series eval) — these are the profile targets the task description asked to identify.
2. **Capstone thread-scaling bench** in the same file: for N in {1, 2, 4, 8}: N threads via std::thread::scope sharing one &Ephemeris (Moshier), each computing a fixed slice of a 10_000-epoch × Sun..Pluto workload; measure wall-clock with `iter_custom`, report throughput (charts/sec) per N. The assertion of interest is near-linear scaling (no hidden synchronization). Print a small table.
3. **tools/bench_c.c**: same four core workloads against `../swisseph/libswe.a` (pattern-match tools/golden_gen.c for includes/linking; add a Makefile target `bench_c`). Timing via clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC), ≥3s warm loop each, print ns/op. Note in comments: C numbers are single-thread only — libswe is not thread-safe; that asymmetry IS the point of the capstone. Run swe_set_ephe_path("../swisseph/ephe") for the Swiss workload.
4. **docs/benchmarks.md**: methodology (hardware line from /proc/cpuinfo model name, rustc/gcc versions, flags), the Rust vs C table for the four workloads, the thread-scaling table, and two honesty notes: (a) C timings exclude any locking a real multi-threaded C consumer would need; (b) first-call file-open costs are excluded in both (setup outside the timed loop).
5. **README Performance section**: 10 lines max — the headline table (Rust vs C, and 8-thread scaling factor) + link to docs/benchmarks.md. Run everything with `cargo bench` on the machine and paste real numbers; do not ship placeholder numbers.

### C reference
tools/golden_gen.c + tools/Makefile as the build pattern for linking libswe.a. Public API only (catalogue-public.md if function signatures needed). No C internals.

### Golden tests
None — benchmarks, not correctness. `cargo test` must stay green after the Cargo.toml edits.

### Acceptance criteria
- `cargo bench` runs all groups to completion
- `make -C tools bench_c && tools/bench_c` runs to completion
- docs/benchmarks.md contains real measured numbers (no TODO/placeholder)
- README has the Performance section
- `cargo test` passes

### Escape hatch
If criterion's harness fights the thread-scaling measurement (iter_custom awkwardness), fall back to a plain `#[bench]`-style manual timing loop inside the same bench binary and report numbers via println — measured honestly beats framework-pretty. If Rust is >2x slower than C on any core workload, don't tune — report the gap with a profile hint (cargo flamegraph target) as a finding; optimization is a separate task.
execution_record: Moshier full-chart is 44× slower than C single-thread due to stateless recomputation of Earth/nutation on every call (C caches globally). This is the expected architectural cost — reported as a finding with a profile hint rather than tuned. Swiss files 2.6× slower, houses 1.8× faster, eclipse ~parity. Thread scaling: 3.4× at 4 threads, 4.2× at 8 threads — near-linear through physical core count, zero synchronization. The 44× Moshier gap is the optimization target for a future epoch-scoped cache task.

edges.note: bench task appends the Performance section to the README 118 creates
